title: Our Ancestors in Us
objective: After this level you can explain which features our bodies inherited from early humans.
summary: Walking upright goes back about 6 million years, big brains came later, and Homo sapiens arose in Africa about 300,000 years ago. Many people also carry 1 to 2 percent Neanderthal DNA.

cards.headline: The design of your lower back is millions of years old.
cards.body: Our species appeared in Africa about 300,000 years ago, but many of your body's features are far older, inherited from earlier humans. Read your body like a family history, starting with the way you stand.

cards.headline: Standing up came first
cards.body: Walking on two legs is the oldest of these inheritances: the oldest evidence for it comes from fossils of the earliest known humans, about 6 million years ago. The curve of your lower back, which absorbs shock with every step, is uniquely human, and a similar curve shows up in the spine of an early human called Australopithecus africanus.

cards.headline: Then the brain grew
cards.body: Big brains came much later. The earliest humans had brains about the size of a chimpanzee's. Over human evolution, brain size tripled, growing fastest during a time of dramatic climate change. Our own species, Homo sapiens, evolved in Africa about 300,000 years ago, carrying that big brain on top of a very old way of walking.

cards.fact: Many people carry some Neanderthal DNA.
cards.context: Svante Pääbo's team published the first Neanderthal genome in 2010 and showed that our species interbred with Neanderthals. For people of European or Asian descent, about 1 to 2 percent of their DNA comes from them. The work won Pääbo the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

cards.headline: A family tree in bone and DNA
cards.body: Fossils and DNA tell the same story: humans are one of more than 200 species of primates, and Neanderthals are our closest extinct relatives. Your body is a patchwork of those inheritances: an upright walker's spine, a big brain, and, for many people, a little Neanderthal.

cards.headline: Our ancestors: found
learned: Walking upright goes back about 6 million years
Brain size tripled over human evolution
Homo sapiens evolved in Africa about 300,000 years ago
About 1 to 2 percent Neanderthal DNA in many people

questions.prompt: Homo sapiens evolved in Africa about _____ ago.

options.label: 3 million years
options.rationale: Far too early for our species.

questions.explanation: Homo sapiens evolved in Africa about 300,000 years ago.

questions.prompt: Put these milestones of human evolution in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Walking on two legs came first, about 6 million years ago; big brains came much later; Homo sapiens evolved about 300,000 years ago; and the first Neanderthal genome was published in 2010.

questions.prompt: Your skeletal system holds you up. Which skeletal feature is uniquely human and absorbs shock when you walk?

options.label: The shape of the jaw
options.rationale: The jaw doesn't absorb shock from walking.

options.label: The number of fingers
options.rationale: Finger count has nothing to do with absorbing shock.

options.label: The size and shape of the skull
The curve of the lower back

questions.explanation: The curve of the lower back absorbs shock when you walk and is uniquely human.
